results.reply:
**Your legal position:**
Airline ka flight cancel karna aur sirf 'credit shell' offer karna, jabki aap refund chahte hain, ek 'deficiency in service' (sewa mein kami) maani ja sakti hai. Consumer Protection Act ke tahat, agar airline ne flight cancel ki hai, toh aap refund ke haqdaar hain; woh aapko zabardasti credit shell lene ke liye majboor nahi kar sakte.

**Law you can cite:**
* **Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(11)):** Yeh 'deficiency in service' ko define karta hai, jismein airline ka refund na dena aur apni marzi thopna shamil hai.
* **Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (Rule 6(3)):** Yeh saaf kehta hai ki agar service mein kami hai, toh seller/provider refund dene se mana nahi kar sakta.

**What to do now:**
1. **National Consumer Helpline (1915):** Sabse pehle yahan complaint register karein, yeh free hai aur aksar airlines yahan se aayi shikayat par jaldi sunwai karti hain.
2. **Formal Email:** Airline ke Nodal Officer ko ek email bhejein jismein saaf likhein ki aapko credit shell nahi, refund chahiye (Consumer Protection Act ka hawala dein).
3. **e-Jagriti Portal:** Agar 15 din mein hal na nikle, toh [e-Jagriti](https://e-jagriti.gov.in/) par online complaint file karein. Ismein koi lawyer ki zaroorat nahi hai aur ₹12,000 ke claim ke liye koi fees bhi nahi hai.

**I need from you:**
1. Kya aapke paas airline ka woh email ya message hai jismein unhone refund dene se mana kiya hai?
2. Aapka city aur state kya hai?

citations.title: Meaning of 'deficiency' in service
citations.plain: A deficiency is any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of a service that the law or a contract requires. It also covers negligence or acts or omissions that cause you loss, and deliberately withholding relevant information from you.

citations.title: Seller/platform cannot refuse return or refund for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods
citations.plain: A seller on a marketplace (rule 6(3)) and an inventory e-commerce entity (rule 7(4)) cannot refuse to take back goods or refuse a refund if the goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or not as advertised. The same applies if delivery was late, unless the delay was due to force majeure.

citations.title: National Consumer Helpline (NCH) contact details
citations.plain: Before going to a Consumer Commission, you can register a complaint free with the National Consumer Helpline. Call 1915 or 1800-11-4000 (toll-free), WhatsApp or SMS +91 8800001915, or file online at consumerhelpline.gov.in. NCH is a pre-litigation mediation channel, not a court, and cannot pass binding orders.

citations.title: e-Jagriti: current portal for filing consumer complaints (replaced e-Daakhil)
citations.plain: Consumer complaints to the District, State and National Commissions are now filed online on e-Jagriti (https://e-jagriti.gov.in/). It launched on 1 January 2025 and merged the older e-Daakhil, OCMS, NCDRC CMS and CONFONET systems. You can file, pay fees, attend virtual hearings and track your case there.

deadlines.label: Last date to file a consumer complaint (2 years from when the problem arose)
deadlines.note: The commission can accept a late complaint only if you show sufficient cause for the delay.

derived.label: Where to file
derived.note: Based on the amount you paid (₹12,000), not the amount you claim.
